phases.name: Walking skeleton — lanes become per-project data (US-BLM-01)

steps.name: Migration 0015 + lane-driven board render (grandfather, cancelled surfacing)
steps.description: Land migration 0015_project_lanes.sql (lanes DDL, idempotent grandfather seed incl. conditional Cancelled, drop CHECK + DEFAULT, add composite FK fk_issues_lane — forward-only, zero issue-row updates per data-models.md). Make Store::list_project_lanes and services board::board_view real; switch board render from DEFAULT_COLUMNS iteration to lane rows (const not yet deleted — 01-02). Sweep other acceptance step modules that seed projects/issues via raw SQL so their fixtures satisfy the new FK.
criteria: Migration 0015 creates lanes, seeds four grandfathered lanes per project (Cancelled only where a cancelled issue exists), swaps CHECK/DEFAULT for composite FK fk_issues_lane; idempotent seed, zero issue-row updates.
Boards without cancelled issues render byte-identically after upgrade; a project holding cancelled issues gains a Cancelled column after Done, showing the previously invisible card.
Board columns derive from Store::list_project_lanes through services board_view (one authz gate); acceptance oracles read lane rows back from the DB, never a static list.
Zero-laneless guard query returns 0 after migration and after every scenario; migration oracle passes staged 0001..0014 then canonical run, executed twice.
Existing suites that seed projects/issues via raw SQL are swept to seed lane rows; full workspace (check, clippy, check-arch, acceptance default lane) stays green.
scenario_name: The upgrade grandfathers every existing board and can run twice safely
Existing boards render unchanged when lanes become data
A long-invisible cancelled issue gets a visible lane
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): PBT (proptest) for new pure logic (classify_lane_delete, leftmost selection, lane validation predicate); single-example only with a # bypass: comment; acceptance = un-pend the DISTILL feature file, never re-author; browser/integration single-example. THIS STEP: EXEMPT — migration SQL, query pass-throughs and template wiring introduce no new pure logic; compensating properties are the run-twice migration oracle (stage_subset(14) + run_migrations_from_dir, executed twice), the FK ADD validating every live row (the migration's built-in probe, architecture-design.md §4), and DB-derived lane oracles. Earned Trust: verify the issues_state_check auto-generated constraint name via pg_constraint on a live-data copy BEFORE relying on the DROP (DISTILL pre-req 1). Seed ids via gen_random_uuid(); labels byte-equal to today's headers (backlog/Backlog/0, todo/Todo/1, in_progress/In-Progress/2, done/Done/3, conditional cancelled/Cancelled/4). Un-pend order: walking-skeleton scenario first.

steps.name: Per-project lane validation live; static lane expressions deleted; check-arch rule
steps.description: Make validate_project_lane real (alias fold then per-project membership — the DD10 single seam) and swap it into change_issue_state so HTML dialog, dnd POST and /api/v1 PATCH accept/refuse identically. Edit-dialog Status options become a loop over IssueEditView.lanes. Delete the now-dead static lane expressions (DEFAULT_COLUMNS, column_label_to_state, hardcoded option list); wire report status labels to live lanes.label with humanize_state fallback for dead slugs. Add the check-arch no-static-lane-list rule (architecture-design.md §8).
criteria: Edit-dialog Status options loop over IssueEditView.lanes in board order; a board with a Cancelled lane offers exactly five options, one without offers four.
validate_project_lane (alias fold, then lane-set membership) sits behind change_issue_state; an unknown lane on HTML dialog, dnd POST or API PATCH is refused 422 invalid_state.
DEFAULT_COLUMNS, column_label_to_state and the hardcoded option list are deleted; report status labels resolve live lanes.label with humanize_state fallback for dead slugs.

cargo xtask check-arch fails any build reintroducing a static lane-slug list under crates/foundry-app/src or crates/foundry-api/src outside #[cfg(test)]; exemptions: store creation seed, humanize_state fallback.
Drag-and-drop lands cards exactly where dropped, persists on reload, and records the status change event — unchanged behavior over data-driven lanes; board-dnd.js and keyboard.js untouched.
scenario_name: The edit dialog offers exactly the board's lanes
A write to a lane the board does not have is refused
Drag-and-drop still lands cards exactly where they are dropped
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): PBT (proptest) for new pure logic (classify_lane_delete, leftmost selection, lane validation predicate); single-example only with a # bypass: comment; acceptance = un-pend the DISTILL feature file, never re-author; browser/integration single-example. PBT TARGET here: the lane-validation predicate — property: for any lane set and any input, validate accepts iff normalized input is a member; alias folding (in-progress→in_progress, canceled→cancelled) is preserved. normalize_state is demoted to a private helper, never removed from the alias-folding role. The check-arch rule follows the slugify-ban idiom; its two exemptions (store creation seed, humanize_state historical fallback) are pinned by architecture-design.md §8 / ADR-BOARD-LANE-001 and must be documented in the rule.

steps.name: Three-lane creation seed; leftmost-lane issue landing; truthful create echo
steps.description: insert_project becomes a transaction that also seeds exactly Backlog, In-Progress, Done (the creation-seed constant lives in foundry-store::lanes — documented exemption). insert_issue_with_outbox resolves the project's leftmost lane inside its transaction, inserts state explicitly (column DEFAULT is gone), and returns InsertedIssue { number, state }; CreatedIssue.state echoes the actual landing slug, replacing the hardcoded "backlog".
criteria: insert_project transactionally seeds exactly backlog/Backlog/0, in_progress/In-Progress/1, done/Done/2; a freshly created board renders exactly those three columns in that order.
insert_issue_with_outbox resolves the leftmost lane (ORDER BY position ASC LIMIT 1) inside its transaction, inserts state explicitly, and returns InsertedIssue carrying the persisted landing slug.
CreatedIssue.state echoes the actual landing slug through the API create reply — the hardcoded "backlog" echo at services/issues.rs:124 is gone.
A new project's edit dialog offers exactly Backlog, In-Progress, Done; the API accepts "in_progress" (200, card moves) and refuses "todo" (422, card unchanged).
If the resolved leftmost lane is deleted concurrently, the insert retries once re-resolving leftmost; a second failure maps to an honest store error, fully rolled back.
scenario_name: A new project's board opens with the three default lanes
The first issue lands in the leftmost lane
The filing reply names the lane the issue actually landed in
The edit dialog of a new project offers exactly the three lanes
The board's lanes bound what any client may set
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): PBT (proptest) for new pure logic (classify_lane_delete, leftmost selection, lane validation predicate); single-example only with a # bypass: comment; acceptance = un-pend the DISTILL feature file, never re-author; browser/integration single-example. PBT TARGET here: leftmost selection — property: for any non-empty lane set, the landing lane is the unique minimum position, independent of insertion order and slugs. Acceptance oracles already derive 'leftmost' from lane rows (position ASC LIMIT 1) — do not weaken them. Three-defaults chain drives the REAL create port (POST /team/{t}/projects), not SQL seeding. The InsertedIssue return-type change ripples to every insert_issue_with_outbox caller; the store creation-seed constant is one of the two check-arch exemptions.

phases.name: Empty-lane deletion behind a confirm dialog (US-BLM-03)

steps.name: Delete-lane dialog GET + confirm POST: empty-lane path, last-lane refusal, authz, CSRF
steps.description: Make the lane routes real: safe GET renders partials/delete_lane_modal.html into #modal-root (empty-lane confirm-only arm); confirm POST executes the empty-lane delete through services delete_lane / classify_lane_delete and the delete_lane_with_fate transaction skeleton (lock lane, last-lane gate, lane-row delete — fate arms trivial for zero cards). Board gains the per-column delete affordance and id="board-columns"; success responds with the OOB column refresh. Last-lane 422 into [data-error-slot]; uniform 404 on both verbs for non-members; CSRF leg on the POST.
criteria: GET lanes/{slug}/delete is a safe read (no _csrf, no writes) rendering the dialog into #modal-root; empty-lane copy: "It holds no issues. This cannot be undone."
Confirmed empty-lane delete removes the lane from board render, dialog options, dnd targets and API validation via the OOB #board-columns swap without full reload; persists across reloads.
Deleting the sole remaining lane returns 422 with exact copy "A board needs at least one lane" routed into [data-error-slot]; the lane survives.
After the leftmost lane is deleted, new issues land in the new leftmost lane.
Non-member GET and POST return the uniform 404 byte-identical to a never-existed path; a tokenless POST is refused by the CSRF middleware; nothing is written.
scenario_name: An empty lane disappears after an explicit confirm
Asking for the confirm dialog changes nothing by itself
The last lane cannot be deleted
New issues follow the leftmost surviving lane
Only team members can delete a lane
A delete that does not carry the board's matching token is refused
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): PBT (proptest) for new pure logic (classify_lane_delete, leftmost selection, lane validation predicate); single-example only with a # bypass: comment; acceptance = un-pend the DISTILL feature file, never re-author; browser/integration single-example. PBT TARGET here: classify_lane_delete partial arms — properties: lane_count==1 always LastLane; lane absent always NotFound; never Proceed when either holds. VERBATIM COPY PINNED (component-boundaries.md §4): last-lane 422 fragment "A board needs at least one lane"; empty-lane dialog "It holds no issues. This cannot be undone."; close is button.modal-close[data-action="close-modal"] ONLY — no new Escape/click listener (BR-4, ADR-MODAL-CLOSE-001). Refusals on lane routes are the uniform resource_not_found_page on BOTH verbs; the lane-route-404 vs board-page-403 asymmetry is chosen (architecture-design.md §10.4). Scraper markers must match component-boundaries §4 exactly (data-modal, data-lane, data-lane-count, data-lane-delete, data-error-slot). The related @needs-browser modal-close scenario is owned by 04-02, keeping this step at 6 scenarios.

phases.name: Two-fate deletion of a populated lane (US-BLM-04)

steps.name: The two-fate write path: move-all / delete-all in one guarded transaction
steps.description: Complete Store::delete_lane_with_fate per ADR-BOARD-LANE-002: one transaction — lock dying lane, last-lane gate, lock destination (move), confirm-time membership FOR UPDATE (position ASC, number DESC), fate arm (move: append positions + one 0013 status event + one IssueUpdated outbox row per card; delete: DELETE WHERE id = ANY(ids), delete_issue_cascade shape), lane-row delete as FK strand-guard, bounded retry (≤3) on foreign_key_violation/deadlock. Complete classify_lane_delete (UnknownDestination arm) and the populated-lane dialog arm (count copy, survivor picker, two fate buttons).
criteria: delete_lane_with_fate is one transaction: lane lock, last-lane gate, confirm-time membership FOR UPDATE, fate arm, lane delete; FK strand-guard with bounded retry (max 3) re-resolving membership.

Move fate appends cards at destination positions C..C+N-1 preserving relative order, writing one 0013 status event (old=dying, new=destination, actor=operator) plus one outbox row per card, same transaction.
Delete fate removes cards permanently via the delete_issue_cascade shape — gone from board and search; no events, no outbox, no tombstone.
Dialog for N>=1 cards states "It holds {N} issues." and offers exactly two fates plus cancel; picker lists survivors in board order, leftmost preselected; cancel leaves everything byte-identical.
A card committed into the dying lane mid-decision is included in the fate at confirm time; zero-laneless guard holds after commit; retry exhaustion returns 500, fully rolled back.
scenario_name: Cards move to the chosen lane and keep their order
Cards are deleted only by an explicit, counted, permanent choice
The prompt offers only surviving lanes as destinations
Walking away from the prompt changes nothing
A card filed mid-decision is still accounted for
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): PBT (proptest) for new pure logic (classify_lane_delete, leftmost selection, lane validation predicate); single-example only with a # bypass: comment; acceptance = un-pend the DISTILL feature file, never re-author; browser/integration single-example. PBT TARGET here: classify_lane_delete complete — properties: Proceed{Move} iff lane exists, count>1, destination in survivors and != dying; destination==dying or absent => UnknownDestination; decision is pure in its inputs. VERBATIM COPY PINNED (component-boundaries.md §4): "It holds {N} issues.", buttons "Move all {N} to …" (fate=move) and "Delete all {N} permanently — this cannot be undone" (fate=delete); 422 fragments (UnknownDestination) route into [data-error-slot]; double-submit race => uniform 404. Earned Trust gold tests (architecture-design.md §8, ADR-BOARD-LANE-002): (1) file an issue into the dying lane between dialog GET and confirm POST, assert zero-laneless guard; (2) crossing A<->B concurrent deletes resolve cleanly — both succeed or one fails cleanly, never partial. The narrower mid-transaction window is documented untestable in-lane (DISTILL oracle discipline #7); a store-level pause-seam test is optional. Mutation >=80% on touched code.

steps.name: Browser lane: fate dialog end-to-end and dialog close, feature closeout
steps.description: Un-pend the two @needs-browser scenarios and drive them green in the fantoccini lane: the full counted fate decision in #modal-root (htmx submitter name/value verified empirically per the Earned Trust table), and dialog close via the declarative data-action mechanism leaving the board alone. Close out the feature: zero @pending remaining, mutation and DoD gates.

Browser: the dialog closes via data-action="close-modal" and Esc through the single Escape owner; the board is untouched after close; no new listeners registered (BR-4).
Both @needs-browser scenarios green in the fantoccini lane (chromedriver probe-then-refuse harness).
Zero @pending scenarios remain in board-lane-management.feature; all 24 green; per-feature mutation >=80% on touched code; cargo xtask ci green.

The delete dialog closes like every other dialog, leaving the board alone
